findings.issue_text: No findings; all four deterministic reviewers passed.
`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-96` — sync returns a native `Response`, but Google reads `res.data`; token refresh fails.
`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-202` — a native `Response` is treated as `HubspotToken` without parsing, producing an undefined token and `NaN` expiry.
`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:67-95` — the generic sync response cannot satisfy Lark’s required nested refresh-token fields.
`packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:62-90` — the generic sync response lacks Webex’s required provider-specific fields and is rejected.
`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-10` — Zod schema objects are incorrectly used as computed property names, so expiry fields are stripped instead of preserved.
`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-26` — a missing refresh token becomes the literal `"refresh_token"`, overwriting valid stored tokens and breaking later refreshes.
`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101` — the entire Zod `SafeParse` wrapper is persisted instead of `.data`, corrupting the credential’s stored shape.
`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96-107` — after refreshing and saving a token, Salesforce constructs its connection with the stale pre-refresh token.
`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-90` — Salesforce bypasses the sync abstraction and refreshes on every client construction, adding unnecessary latency and rate-limit usage.
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-70` — `(userId, appId)` is assumed unique without an enforced invariant; `findFirst` can update an arbitrary external-account credential.
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61-90` — check-then-create is neither transactional nor protected by a unique constraint, so concurrent deliveries can create duplicate credentials.
`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59` — any accepted team member can create a team-wide credential; the admin-access guard is bypassed by the team branch.
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17-31,56-59` — unsupported methods and malformed bodies, ciphertext, or JSON are allowed to throw as 500 responses instead of controlled 4xx errors.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14` — HIGH/A01-A07: token-sync requests send only guessable user and app identifiers with no authentication, permitting unauthorized token retrieval from an endpoint implementing this contract.
`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` — the refactor replaces the configuration-derived callback slug with a hard-coded path, introducing an unnecessary second source of truth.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-18` — no tests cover feature toggling, user/team ownership, malformed or non-2xx sync responses, provider response contracts, or refresh-persist-reload behavior.

Review note: the stable checkout contains only base `4380f3a` and PR `9140052`, so literal `HEAD~2` became invalid after scaffold generation; all six lenses reviewed the equivalent stable PR range `4380f3a..9140052`.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-202` — a native `Response` is treated as `HubspotToken` without parsing, producing an undefined token and `NaN` expiry.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the existing hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken call with refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) either calls the provided refreshFunction and returns its result, OR makes a fetch call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and returns the fetch Response object. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, the function returns a raw fetch Response, not the parsed HubspotToken. The code then treats this as HubspotToken directly (hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn, hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken, etc.), which would be undefined on a Response object, causing NaN expiry and undefined tokens. This is a real bug in the credential sync path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:67-95` — the generic sync response cannot satisfy Lark’s required nested refresh-token fields.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (lines 3-21 in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) either calls the provided refreshFunction or makes a request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. When credential sync is enabled, it returns the response from the sync endpoint directly. The original Lark code expects to call handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log) on line 85 which expects a specific Lark response format with nested fields. If the sync endpoint returns a generic OAuth response format, it won't have Lark's specific nested structure (like data.refresh_token, data.access_token etc. that RefreshTokenResp likely expects). This is a valid concern - the sync response format may not match Lark's expected response structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-70` — `(userId, appId)` is assumed unique without an enforced invariant; `findFirst` can update an arbitrary external-account credential.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 62-70, the code uses `findFirst` to find a credential by `userId` and `appId`. The concern is that without a unique constraint on (userId, appId), there could be multiple credentials matching these criteria, and `findFirst` would return an arbitrary one. However, examining the code logic: this is a webhook endpoint for syncing app credentials from an external system. The code checks if a credential exists for a user+app combination and either updates it or creates a new one. In the Cal.com data model, it's reasonable to expect that a user would have at most one credential per app (the business logic suggests this). While a unique database constraint would be safer, the code's behavior of updating 'the first found' credential when there should logically only be one is not necessarily a bug - it's a design choice. The finding raises a valid concern about potential data integrity issues if multiple credentials exist, but this is more of a defensive programming suggestion than a clear bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61-90` — check-then-create is neither transactional nor protected by a unique constraint, so concurrent deliveries can create duplicate credentials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lines 61-90 in the webhook handler, there's a findFirst followed by either update or create. The code checks if a credential exists for (userId, appId), then either updates or creates. Without a unique constraint on (userId, appId) in the database or transaction isolation, two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app could both pass the findFirst check (returning null), then both attempt to create, resulting in duplicate credentials. This is a real race condition - the check-then-act pattern without proper synchronization is a classic concurrency bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14` — HIGH/A01-A07: token-sync requests send only guessable user and app identifiers with no authentication, permitting unauthorized token retrieval from an endpoint implementing this contract.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 8-14, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it sends a POST request with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. There is no authentication header, secret, or signature included in this outbound request. The comment says 'Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires' but the default implementation has no authentication. However, this is an OUTBOUND request to an external endpoint that the self-hoster controls - it's not an incoming webhook. The security of this depends on the external endpoint's implementation. The finding claims this 'permits unauthorized token retrieval' but the external endpoint is controlled by the self-hoster who would implement their own authentication. This is a design choice for flexibility, not necessarily a vulnerability in Cal.com's code itself. The real security concern would be if the external endpoint doesn't authenticate, but that's outside this codebase.
